ai.description: This small frog (20–25 mm) is brown with a dark lateral band. Males display a distinctive foot-flagging behavior, extending and waving their hind limbs to attract mates near fast-flowing streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus saxicola* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright orange-to-reddish throat patch in males, which contrasts sharply with its otherwise brownish body.
ai.habitat: The Wayanad Dancing Frog inhabits fast-flowing, rocky streams within evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: To attract mates, male *Micrixalus saxicola* perform "foot-flagging," extending and waving their hind legs in a rhythmic display above the rushing water of forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus saxicola* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in nests excavated under stream-bed gravel. They exhibit terrestrial-aquatic larval development.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Wayanad dancing frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting streams in Kerala and Karnataka at elevations between 700 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Wayanad Dancing Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes while calling from the rocky, fast-flowing streams of its forest habitat.
